why: Text Completion is one of the two sentence-completion types that together make up about half of the Verbal measure, and how an item is built and scored shapes how you answer it.
rule:
A passage runs from **1 to 5 sentences** and contains **1 to 3 blanks**.

- **One blank:** five choices.
- **Two or three blanks:** three choices for each blank.
- Every blank has exactly one correct answer, and the columns are independent: choosing one entry does not remove any entry from another column.
- There is **no partial credit**: all blanks must be right.

Each blank is decided by the rest of the text: look for a phrase that restates it, or a word that signals a contrast (*although*, *far from*, *anything but*) or a result (*because*, *so ... that*).

examples.prompt: The critic's early reviews were (i)______, praising nearly every film; her later reviews were far more (ii)______, rarely finding anything to admire.  (i) lenient | cryptic | hurried;  (ii) severe | affectionate | repetitive.
steps: Count: two blanks, so three choices each; both must be right for any credit.
Blank (i): "praising nearly every film" means going easy: *lenient*.
Blank (ii): "rarely finding anything to admire" is the opposite: *severe*.
Re-read: early reviews lenient, later ones severe. The contrast is coherent.

trap: Assuming a half-right answer scores something. It does not: every blank must be correct, so settle the blank you are unsure about by re-reading the whole sentence.

checks.stem: Select one entry from the choices that best completes the text.
checks.explanation: **Result clue:** *so ... that even the youngest grasped it at once*. Only a clear explanation does that: *lucid*.

choiceExplanations.B: Boring does not mean easily understood.
choiceExplanations.C: Dodging the question would not teach anyone.

content.text: Her explanation was so {{1}} that even the youngest students grasped the idea at once.

checks.stem: For each blank select one entry from the corresponding column of choices. Fill all blanks in the way that best completes the text.
checks.explanation: **Structure:** two blanks, three choices each. *Only twelve patients* gives *narrow*; *so* ... *about claiming* ... *everyone* gives restraint: *cautious*.

choiceExplanations.1C: Twelve patients is not a broad scope.
choiceExplanations.1B: Means extravagant; it does not describe scope.
choiceExplanations.2C: A reckless author would claim too much.

content.text: The study was {{1}} in scope, covering only twelve patients, so its authors were {{2}} about claiming that the results applied to everyone.

checks.stem: For each blank select one entry from the corresponding column of choices. Fill all blanks in the way that best completes the text.
checks.explanation: **Three blanks, easiest first.** *Though ... rain* needs a negative: *marred*. *Optimism* and record crowds give *hopeful* and *justified*.

choiceExplanations.1A: Rain does not improve a festival; *though* needs a setback.
choiceExplanations.1B: Being ignored by rain makes no sense.
choiceExplanations.2C: The sentence calls them optimistic, not indifferent.
choiceExplanations.3B: Record crowds prove the optimism right.
choiceExplanations.3A: Record crowds show the optimism served a purpose.

content.text: Though the first day of the festival was {{1}} by rain, the organizers stayed {{2}}, and when sunshine brought record crowds by the weekend, their optimism proved {{3}}.
